text:
PagerDuty Case Study | Instrument
PagerDuty
This is tagged with: brand, marketing
PagerDuty is the operations engine behind the tech we rely on everyday, like Netflix, Zoom, and Chipotle. As a trusted partner for these brands, PagerDuty is driven by their mission to revolutionize operations and deliver seamless digital experiences — which is why they built the Operations Cloud platform. To help spread the word about this broader platform, we created a bold brand campaign for starting candid conversations with C-level leaders.
The Challenge 
Getting on the radar of Enterprise decision makers and drastically changing how they viewed the brand’s capabilities.
pagerduty_stackedcomputers_v2 from Instrument on Vimeo 
Exploring the mind of a Chief Technology Officer
Leaders today are under enormous pressure to drive growth and cut costs. Operational excellence is no longer a “nice to have” — it’s essential for survival. 
Yet, when researching for the campaign, we learned many companies were stuck on their path to digital transformation. Leaders described their operations as a tangled mess of homegrown solutions and one-too-many tools, leaving teams buried under inefficient workflows. 
A recessionary environment had dialed up the urgency to intervene. Leaders felt this was finally the moment for an overhaul. With that insight, we knew we could craft a campaign that would resonate emotionally and point them to a platform that could help.
The Idea
Delivering urgent truths about the state of business to execs through frank headlines and a bold, activation-ready palette.
Building a flexible creative toolkit
In developing the campaign, we needed to stay true to PagerDuty’s fun personality while introducing sophistication to earn trust as a serious competitor. 
Drawing on the sense of urgency discovered in our research, we paired punchy, sharp-witted headlines with a new bold color we call Volt that evokes emotion and stands out in crowded feeds. We created a series of illustrations inspired by graphic styles used in instruction manuals and emergency communications — balancing feelings of familiarity, empathy, and just a little levity. 
All the elements came together as a system of visuals and messaging designed to flex and scale across a wide variety of channels and formats, from hard-working digital assets to high-visibility OOH and events.
The Impact
Shifting PagerDuty from a product to a platform built for modern enterprise — and catapulting their next phase of growth.
A successful launch and reception
The campaign launched at re:Invent 2023, and a coordinated rollout will continue into 2024, fueling an exciting and monumental year for PagerDuty. 
So far, the campaign has outperformed previous brand campaigns by 37%, with messaging resonating strongest with C-suite audiences. The “Operations Intervention” messaging has been adopted across the website and sales teams, creating a thoughtful through line for customers across the brand experience.
It has been so exciting to move our business forward with a distinctive, original campaign that both expanded the frame of reference for the PagerDuty brand and stayed true to our roots. Ops Intervention is engaging our customers, inspiring our teams, and raising the bar for how we show up at the intersection of strategy and creativity.

# PagerDuty Case Study | Instrument

PagerDuty

This is tagged with: brand, marketing

#### PagerDuty is the operations engine behind the tech we rely on everyday, like Netflix, Zoom, and Chipotle. As a trusted partner for these brands, PagerDuty is driven by their mission to revolutionize operations and deliver seamless digital experiences — which is why they built the Operations Cloud platform. To help spread the word about this broader platform, we created a bold brand campaign for starting candid conversations with C-level leaders.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/10148x6777/f9f63122c0/pagerduty-hero-1.png/m/)

#### The Challenge

#### Getting on the radar of Enterprise decision makers and drastically changing how they viewed the brand’s capabilities.

   pagerduty\_stackedcomputers\_v2 from Instrument on Vimeo

**Exploring the mind of a Chief Technology Officer**

Leaders today are under enormous pressure to drive growth and cut costs. Operational excellence is no longer a “nice to have” — it’s essential for survival.

Yet, when researching for the campaign, we learned many companies were stuck on their path to digital transformation. Leaders described their operations as a tangled mess of homegrown solutions and one-too-many tools, leaving teams buried under inefficient workflows.

A recessionary environment had dialed up the urgency to intervene. Leaders felt this was finally the moment for an overhaul. With that insight, we knew we could craft a campaign that would resonate emotionally and point them to a platform that could help.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/2160x428/afc3cb010f/image-1.png/m/)

#### The Idea

#### Delivering urgent truths about the state of business to execs through frank headlines and a bold, activation-ready palette.

**Building a flexible creative toolkit**

In developing the campaign, we needed to stay true to PagerDuty’s fun personality while introducing sophistication to earn trust as a serious competitor.

Drawing on the sense of urgency discovered in our research, we paired punchy, sharp-witted headlines with a new bold color we call Volt that evokes emotion and stands out in crowded feeds. We created a series of illustrations inspired by graphic styles used in instruction manuals and emergency communications — balancing feelings of familiarity, empathy, and just a little levity.

All the elements came together as a system of visuals and messaging designed to flex and scale across a wide variety of channels and formats, from hard-working digital assets to high-visibility OOH and events.

#### The Impact

#### Shifting PagerDuty from a product to a platform built for modern enterprise — and catapulting their next phase of growth.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/5760x2949/a4be2747fa/image-2.png/m/)

**A successful launch and reception**

The campaign launched at re:Invent 2023, and a coordinated rollout will continue into 2024, fueling an exciting and monumental year for PagerDuty.

So far, the campaign has outperformed previous brand campaigns by 37%, with messaging resonating strongest with C-suite audiences. The “Operations Intervention” messaging has been adopted across the website and sales teams, creating a thoughtful through line for customers across the brand experience.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/1809x1827/cf9852c3ef/pagerduty-ooh-3.png/m/)

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/2724x1821/259a54a19a/pagerduty-ooh-2.png/m/)

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/2724x1821/6f7c2edff0/pagerduty-ooh-1.png/m/)

> It has been so exciting to move our business forward with a distinctive, original campaign that both expanded the frame of reference for the PagerDuty brand and stayed true to our roots. Ops Intervention is engaging our customers, inspiring our teams, and raising the bar for how we show up at the intersection of strategy and creativity.

### Our Role

#### STRATEGY

*   Integrated Marketing Strategy
*   Audience Research
*   Creative Strategy
*   Messaging

#### CREATIVE

*   Campaign Concept
*   Art Direction
*   Visual Design
*   Illustration
*   Copywriting
*   Design Guidelines

Google Holiday 100 | Instrument
Google Holiday 100
This is tagged with: marketing
The Holiday 100 is an annual gift guide inspired by real-time Google Search trends. To make it stand out during the busy holiday shopping season, we created a distinctive, branded shopping experience that seamlessly connects inspiration and e-commerce, helping shoppers discover and purchase the perfect presents.
HO100_Web_Asset_new from Instrument on Vimeo 
The Challenge
Cut through the holiday shopping noise with a shoppable editorial experience for this year’s top trending products.
A merrier, brighter take on holiday gift guides
We viewed the Holiday 100 as a chance to reimagine the traditional gift guide, transforming it into an editorial, story-driven e-commerce experience. By blending custom photography, print materials, and social assets, we created a curated holiday journey that embodied the season's spirit and inspired gift-givers around the world.
This ambitious project was a true collaborative effort, involving Google teams, partner agencies, 100 products, and celebrity talent. Together, we produced and launched hundreds of tailored assets across key holiday milestones, delivering a seamless and engaging experience at every touchpoint.
HO100_Photo_Assets_FINAL from Instrument on Vimeo 
The Idea
Let Search trends lead the way, taking the iconic Google brand into bold, vibrant new territory.
Navigating the blizzard of holiday gift guides
To set the Holiday 100 apart, we anchored it in real-time Google Search data, creating a unique narrative. Guided by real trends, shoppers could trust the marketplace's recommendations. Powered by billions of searches throughout the year, this is a story only Google Shopping could tell.
We harnessed the power of recognizable Google brand elements to create a visually compelling, holiday-inspired look that felt both elevated and accessible to users and stakeholders alike. We paired Google's brand typography with a modern serif to create a sophisticated yet approachable look, and a vibrant holiday color palette and dynamic imagery allowed the products to take center stage.
Holiday 100 custom color palette
Typography setting
Google 2024 Top Trend product badge
Turning up the holiday sparkle
Our photography approach worked seamlessly with the visual system to give the 100-product lineup a cohesive, curated feel. We blended festive celebration with everyday authenticity, showcasing each product in relatable yet aspirational settings. With candid moments, warm lighting, and holiday touches, we captured the joy of the season. To drive engagement, we released eye-catching social GIFs that drew attention and encouraged clicks.
Guiding users through an e-comm wonderland
For the first time, the Holiday 100 was featured on Google’s new Shopping platform, offering a unique opportunity to blend an exciting holiday experience directly within the shopping journey. With products instantly shoppable, the platform connects users to the best deals, reviews, and trusted retailers, making it easier than ever to find and purchase top gifts with confidence.
To enhance the experience, we leveraged Search trends to guide users, highlighting them with a fun, engaging tone throughout the page. A modular design approach was used to simplify and organize the shopping flow, ensuring a seamless and enjoyable experience from start to finish.
Snowballing our concept, expanding our reach
Reaching our largest audience required us to think beyond the site, so we invited even more shoppers into the Holiday 100 experience through a targeted, multi-channel approach. We created dynamic templates to speak to multiple audiences across publications like ELLE, Esquire, Harper’s BAZAAR, and House Beautiful. We also crafted an editorial journey that spanned three key shopping weeks in the New York Times. Our reach extends across social platforms with fresh, dynamic content designed to showcase our featured products and connect with audiences wherever they are.
Putting a bow on it
The Google Holiday 100 evolved into more than a shopping destination–it became a source of inspiration. Drawing together the best gift ideas from billions of annual searches, our campaign experience serves early shoppers, trend seekers, and last minute gift grabbers worldwide.

# Google Holiday 100 | Instrument

### Google Holiday 100

This is tagged with: marketing

#### The Holiday 100 is an annual gift guide inspired by real-time Google Search trends. To make it stand out during the busy holiday shopping season, we created a distinctive, branded shopping experience that seamlessly connects inspiration and e-commerce, helping shoppers discover and purchase the perfect presents.

   HO100\_Web\_Asset\_new from Instrument on Vimeo

### The Challenge

#### Cut through the holiday shopping noise with a shoppable editorial experience for this year’s top trending products.

A merrier, brighter take on holiday gift guides

We viewed the Holiday 100 as a chance to reimagine the traditional gift guide, transforming it into an editorial, story-driven e-commerce experience. By blending custom photography, print materials, and social assets, we created a curated holiday journey that embodied the season's spirit and inspired gift-givers around the world.

This ambitious project was a true collaborative effort, involving Google teams, partner agencies, 100 products, and celebrity talent. Together, we produced and launched hundreds of tailored assets across key holiday milestones, delivering a seamless and engaging experience at every touchpoint.

   HO100\_Photo\_Assets\_FINAL from Instrument on Vimeo

### The Idea

#### Let Search trends lead the way, taking the iconic Google brand into bold, vibrant new territory.

**Navigating the blizzard of holiday gift guides**

To set the Holiday 100 apart, we anchored it in real-time Google Search data, creating a unique narrative. Guided by real trends, shoppers could trust the marketplace's recommendations. Powered by billions of searches throughout the year, this is a story only Google Shopping could tell.

We harnessed the power of recognizable Google brand elements to create a visually compelling, holiday-inspired look that felt both elevated and accessible to users and stakeholders alike. We paired Google's brand typography with a modern serif to create a sophisticated yet approachable look, and a vibrant holiday color palette and dynamic imagery allowed the products to take center stage.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/576x576/6736da7971/color.png/m/)

Holiday 100 custom color palette

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/576x576/4d0c0a82f3/type.png/m/)

Typography setting

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/576x576/d25485c08c/badge.png/m/)

Google 2024 Top Trend product badge

**Turning up the holiday sparkle**

Our photography approach worked seamlessly with the visual system to give the 100-product lineup a cohesive, curated feel. We blended festive celebration with everyday authenticity, showcasing each product in relatable yet aspirational settings. With candid moments, warm lighting, and holiday touches, we captured the joy of the season. To drive engagement, we released eye-catching social GIFs that drew attention and encouraged clicks.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/1919x1176/5db6deca11/google_ho100_static_full.png/m/)

Guiding users through an e-comm wonderland

For the first time, the Holiday 100 was featured on Google’s new Shopping platform, offering a unique opportunity to blend an exciting holiday experience directly within the shopping journey. With products instantly shoppable, the platform connects users to the best deals, reviews, and trusted retailers, making it easier than ever to find and purchase top gifts with confidence.

To enhance the experience, we leveraged Search trends to guide users, highlighting them with a fun, engaging tone throughout the page. A modular design approach was used to simplify and organize the shopping flow, ensuring a seamless and enjoyable experience from start to finish.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/884x1049/f57bc1e137/google_ho100_web_mock.png/m/)

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/884x1049/4564b422d4/google_ho100_web_mock2.png/m/)

**Snowballing our concept, expanding our reach**

Reaching our largest audience required us to think beyond the site, so we invited even more shoppers into the Holiday 100 experience through a targeted, multi-channel approach. We created dynamic templates to speak to multiple audiences across publications like ELLE, Esquire, Harper’s BAZAAR, and House Beautiful. We also crafted an editorial journey that spanned three key shopping weeks in the New York Times. Our reach extends across social platforms with fresh, dynamic content designed to showcase our featured products and connect with audiences wherever they are.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/1920x1080/35a49d85b6/ho100_print_mock.png/m/)

**Putting a bow on it**

The Google Holiday 100 evolved into more than a shopping destination–it became a source of inspiration. Drawing together the best gift ideas from billions of annual searches, our campaign experience serves early shoppers, trend seekers, and last minute gift grabbers worldwide.

> collective of thoughtful, strategic, and  
> creative partners who helped us bring the  
> Holiday 100 to life within a new and  
> delightful consumer experience across our  
> entire marketing activation.

Microsoft Unlocked | Instrument
Microsoft Unlocked
This is tagged with: brand, marketing
Microsoft, a global brand committed to empowering people and organizations to achieve more, partnered with us to create a platform that showcases human stories highlighting technology’s positive impact. We bring these narratives to life on Microsoft Unlocked, creating interactive experiences, leveraging generative AI, and producing photography and films that illustrate the transformative power of technology.
Msft_sizzle-reel-GB_v04_0225 from Instrument on Vimeo 
Msft_sizzle-reel-GB_v04_0225 from Instrument on Vimeo 
Developing stories together
To bring each narrative to life, we collaborate closely, shaping a unique approach to each story and finding the most meaningful way to tell it. From concept to execution, we bring together the right team—blending expertise in content production, AI, UX design, and development—to craft seamless, engaging experiences where ideas shine.
A symphony of AI and the Amazon rainforest
Certain stories are best told through interactive and immersive formats. One example is a story on bioacoustics research in the Amazon, where scientists use Microsoft AI to monitor the health of the ecosystem. Inspired by the rich sounds of the rainforest, we developed a concept built around its natural "symphony.” The result was an experience that invited audiences to step into the researchers' world, engaging with the sights and sounds of the Amazon in a deeply immersive way.
0
MSFT_Unlocked_Bioacoustics_Gallery-Cicada from Instrument on Vimeo 
MSFT_Unlocked_Bioacoustics_LeftRail-Butterfly from Instrument on Vimeo 
A story of rural hospitals and cybersecurity
Video is oftentimes the most powerful way to capture human perspectives and the scope of their impact. When exploring cybersecurity’s role in rural hospitals, we knew this format would best convey the real-world stakes. With that in mind, we set out to tell a deeply personal narrative, planning and producing a photo and video story that put human experiences at the center. The outcome wasn’t just a story—it was a vivid, multi-perspective journey through the eyes of patients, healthcare workers, and IT professionals, showing how Microsoft partners with small communities to keep vital services running when it matters most.
Expanding neuroinclusion in employment
Many of the stories we’ve told center on authentic, human-centered narratives. In our exploration of neurodiversity, we shared the story of Mentra, a platform using Microsoft’s technology to connect neurodivergent individuals with meaningful job opportunities. Through thoughtful photo and video production, we didn’t just highlight the platform—we captured the real journeys of those it serves, including their founders. The result was a powerful depiction of how AI enables Mentra scale its mission, breaking down employment barriers and creating career pathways that truly fit neurodivergent talent.
Bringing complex concepts to life visually
Big ideas—like cybersecurity, biomimicry, or cancer screenings—become more tangible when turned into immersive visuals. Microsoft and Instrument share a belief that technology is most powerful when it serves people, and understanding it is key to unlocking its full potential. Through interactive design, data visualization and art, we help break down complex concepts into experiences that are not just informative, but intuitive and engaging.
0
Short Form Case Study 2_1 from Instrument on Vimeo 
Putting people at the center
Our work brings the Microsoft mission to life—not by focusing on technology alone, but by highlighting the people it empowers. By balancing raw human portraiture with compelling representations of technology and data, we create narratives that reveal the deep connection between innovation and impact. From the halls of Howard University to the nurses in Show Low, Arizona, capturing these stories has been an honor.
Amplifying stories across channels
Beyond designing, writing, and building features for the Unlocked platform—we ensure they reach the right audiences in meaningful ways. Through strategic go-to-market materials and channel-right assets, we tailor content to meet people where they are, whether on social media, at Microsoft events, or beyond. This approach helps amplify the voices of incredible people and communities, ensuring their stories not only inspire but also engage and connect across a wide range of platforms.

Since its launch, the stories we’ve developed on Microsoft Unlocked have driven some of the platform’s highest engagement to date—and that’s just the beginning. This work has also earned industry recognition, with awards celebrating both the platform’s usability and the depth and impact of the stories it shares.

Through thoughtful photo and video production, we didn’t just highlight the platform—we captured the real journeys of those it serves, including their founders. The result was a powerful depiction of how AI enables Mentra scale its mission, breaking down employment barriers and creating career pathways that truly fit neurodivergent talent.

**Bringing complex concepts to life visually**

Big ideas—like cybersecurity, biomimicry, or cancer screenings—become more tangible when turned into immersive visuals. Microsoft and Instrument share a belief that technology is most powerful when it serves people, and understanding it is key to unlocking its full potential. Through interactive design, data visualization and art, we help break down complex concepts into experiences that are not just informative, but intuitive and engaging.

Nike Year in Review | Instrument
This is tagged with: brand, product
“Year in Review” is a personalized and holistic experience for Nike members that celebrated what they achieved in 2023, and also set intentions for the year ahead. We partnered with Nike to break the mold of the typical brand recap. Together, we went beyond reflecting past behavior and instead used that data to deliver insights that prompted reflection, inspiration and action for the future.
Nike_YIR_CS-1_3_1 from Instrument on Vimeo 
A foundational partnership
For over 15 years, we’ve been part of a close and collaborative partnership with Nike—creating digital experiences and content across their apps, dot com, and social extensions. We have a track record of helping the brand tackle some of their most challenging digital briefs and this was one of those opportunities. 
02 Year In Review Imagery from Instrument on Vimeo 
The Opportunity:
Reimagine the year-in-review formula to build a deeper 
ongoing connection with Nike's most loyal athletes.
Creating a holistic, grounding experience for members
Through member-focused exploration and experimentation, we landed on an off-platform solution that allowed us to leverage and reflect data in new and interesting ways. We didn’t just recycle patterns and behaviors around movement and product, but pulled out insights and asked questions that offered real value for members. Working within Nike’s Well Collective look and feel, we used blurred type, grainy textures, and translucent UI to build an experience that was compelling, vibrant, and most of all, inspiring. To bridge the digital and the physical, we started with a grounding moment of deep breathing, helping members get centered for their journey. 
The Differentiator:
Nike isn’t just looking back, it’s moving ahead and positioning 
itself as a partner in their members’ upcoming goals.
Inspiration driven by insights
Our overall aim was to design and build a journey that opened up a two-way conversation with our most loyal members, allowing us to re-engage in the coming year through personalized stories, products, prompts and experiences to help them achieve their future goals. A new look, a fresh workout, more meditation time, building community—we expanded our idea of personal growth to go beyond the typical metrics and activities for more well-rounded and inclusive intention-setting.
The Experience:
Built from the ground up to be personal and dynamic, our 360 
Playbook ensured a seamless rollout to reach members across 
the globe. 
Fine-tuning the moment for a global audience
Tokyo to London, Mexico City to Seoul—to connect with our members in every region, the entire body of work and strategy was adapted into a 360 Global Playbook that enabled Nike teams around the world to execute the ‘Year In Review’ experience for their own members. This included an entire campaign of content and drivers that seamlessly migrated users to the microsite… and back. To create a ‘closed loop’ journey, we used rewards, recommended workouts and unique product offerings to re-engage them on Nike platforms for new goals, self improvement, style and sweat.
In-house development brings the vision to life
Working in lockstep with design and strategy, the development team implemented the technology, architecture and componentry that ensured an elevated user experience and prioritized security and accessibility. 
To achieve these goals, the site was divided into three regions—North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific—and AWS was utilized for routing and caching. Additionally, our dev team managed the records of 21 million Nike members with automated multi-region replication and CI/CD pipelines, all orchestrated through GitHub Actions and Terraform. Localization efforts spanned 14 languages (21 locales) and employed JSON files translated by Nike's Localization team. The front-end was powered by React + Remix using GSAP as our core animation library, while authentication relied on Nike's OIDC provider. All development was WCAG AA 2.1 compliant. Knowing the site would receive a ton of traffic in a short time, we prepared by load testing a million requests a minute before launch day and our architecture stood up to the challenge.
From A-listers to everyday athletes, we saw Nike’s “Year In Review” spread organically far beyond the initial launch moment.

#### “Year in Review” is a personalized and holistic experience for Nike members that celebrated what they achieved in 2023, and also set intentions for the year ahead. We partnered with Nike to break the mold of the typical brand recap. Together, we went beyond reflecting past behavior and instead used that data to deliver insights that prompted reflection, inspiration and action for the future.

   Nike\_YIR\_CS-1\_3\_1 from Instrument on Vimeo

## A foundational partnership

For over 15 years, we’ve been part of a close and collaborative partnership with Nike—creating digital experiences and content across their apps, dot com, and social extensions. We have a track record of helping the brand tackle some of their most challenging digital briefs and this was one of those opportunities. 

   02 Year In Review Imagery from Instrument on Vimeo

#### The Opportunity:

Reimagine the year-in-review formula to build a deeper

ongoing connection with Nike's most loyal athletes.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/1920x1080/355a762e37/media_-cinema.png/m/)

## Creating a holistic, grounding experience for members

Through member-focused exploration and experimentation, we landed on an off-platform solution that allowed us to leverage and reflect data in new and interesting ways. We didn’t just recycle patterns and behaviors around movement and product, but pulled out insights and asked questions that offered real value for members. Working within Nike’s Well Collective look and feel, we used blurred type, grainy textures, and translucent UI to build an experience that was compelling, vibrant, and most of all, inspiring. To bridge the digital and the physical, we started with a grounding moment of deep breathing, helping members get centered for their journey. 

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/1920x1166/c3a0a736db/xxl.png/m/)

#### The Differentiator:

Nike isn’t just looking back, it’s moving ahead and positioning

itself as a partner in their members’ upcoming goals.

## Inspiration driven by insights

Our overall aim was to design and build a journey that opened up a two-way conversation with our most loyal members, allowing us to re-engage in the coming year through personalized stories, products, prompts and experiences to help them achieve their future goals. A new look, a fresh workout, more meditation time, building community—we expanded our idea of personal growth to go beyond the typical metrics and activities for more well-rounded and inclusive intention-setting.

#### The Experience:

Built from the ground up to be personal and dynamic, our 360

Playbook ensured a seamless rollout to reach members across

the globe.

## Fine-tuning the moment for a global audience

Tokyo to London, Mexico City to Seoul—to connect with our members in every region, the entire body of work and strategy was adapted into a 360 Global Playbook that enabled Nike teams around the world to execute the ‘Year In Review’ experience for their own members. This included an entire campaign of content and drivers that seamlessly migrated users to the microsite… and back. To create a ‘closed loop’ journey, we used rewards, recommended workouts and unique product offerings to re-engage them on Nike platforms for new goals, self improvement, style and sweat.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/3840x2360/6c986cde6f/nike-yir-mockup-godso-1-1.jpg/m/)

## In-house development brings the vision to life

Working in lockstep with design and strategy, the development team implemented the technology, architecture and componentry that ensured an elevated user experience and prioritized security and accessibility.

To achieve these goals, the site was divided into three regions—North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific—and AWS was utilized for routing and caching. Additionally, our dev team managed the records of 21 million Nike members with automated multi-region replication and CI/CD pipelines, all orchestrated through GitHub Actions and Terraform. Localization efforts spanned 14 languages (21 locales) and employed JSON files translated by Nike's Localization team. The front-end was powered by React + Remix using GSAP as our core animation library, while authentication relied on Nike's OIDC provider. All development was WCAG AA 2.1 compliant. Knowing the site would receive a ton of traffic in a short time, we prepared by load testing a million requests a minute before launch day and our architecture stood up to the challenge.

From A-listers to everyday athletes,  we saw Nike’s “Year In Review” spread organically far beyond the initial  launch moment.

text:
Qatar Airways | Instrument
Qatar Airways
This is tagged with: product, brand
Qatar Airways is the world’s fastest-growing airline, with over 170 destinations. They came to Instrument with an aspiration to offer the best airline app in the world — one that handled this magnitude of flights, up-leveled their user experience, and evolved the digital application of their brand. Our goal was to create a true “travel companion,” whose elegance matched their on-board luxury experience.
QatarAirway_Case Study_Hero_60fps from Instrument on Vimeo 
The Ask
Reimagining the future of Qatar Airways by 
transforming their fastest-growing channel.
Defining what matters most
Drawing from our expertise in research and testing, we set out to define the ideal set of features for the app. In-depth interviews of stakeholders from every part of Qatar Airways’ complex business infrastructure provided us with a thorough understanding of the company’s business and innovation opportunities. User surveys gauged the needs of a wide swath of Qatar Airways customers. 

Keeping the needs of our global customer base top-of-mind, we conducted multiple rounds of user testing throughout the design process — across seven time zones — to ensure our final feature set would transcend cultural boundaries.
The Approach
Placing our audience at the center of it all with traveler-centric strategy, 
design, and testing.
Embracing the journey
A traveler’s journey begins long before and extends far beyond the day of the flight, so we set out to ensure every touchpoint of their experience was considered. We created customer journeys that mapped needs, behaviors, and mindsets to app features, outlining how our app could anticipate a traveler’s needs at every point. 

With an opportunity to extend the brand’s elegance and ensure the app reflected the premium quality of Qatar Airways’ in-flight experience, we established a new set of experience principles and design tenets to speak directly to travelers — featuring a color palette inspired by sunsets and cabin lighting, aspirational photography from the traveler’s POV, and silky smooth motion transitions.
Testing by trying
Working shoulder-to-shoulder with our designers and strategists, our creative technologists developed a rich, high fidelity iOS prototype to demonstrate new interaction concepts and updated transitions. This ability to test user experience and design decisions in business-critical areas of the app allowed us to iterate rapidly towards the best solutions. 

Throughout component creation, our worldwide audience was top of mind. Designing to platform-specific best practices, we scaled our system to work on both iOS and Android in order to ensure parity of experience, while taking advantage of the best of native functionality. Targeting Qatar Airways’ global, largely Arabic-native customer base, we designed for both left-to-right and right-to-left language considerations.
The Impact
Creating the most intuitive airline app in existence with the ability to serve a 
global audience.
Crossing cultural borders
Partnering with an international airline client fell at a challenging time for travel — right amid a global pandemic. With our teams collaborating halfway around the world, we defined an app that is more intuitive, engaging, and contextually relevant than any other airline app in existence.

Following delivery in 2020, the brand evolution has been so well received that it is currently being applied to transform the Qatar Airways web experience and other marketing channels to serve the unique needs of their global audience.

How to Grow an Agency with Purpose
How to Grow an Agency 
with Purpose
Proof
that
agencies
can
scale
without
sacrifice.
In an industry fixated on speed and scale, the real challenge isn’t growing, it’s growing without compromise. Many agencies focus on getting as big as possible, as quickly as possible. Not only is that approach not sustainable, it prioritizes the wrong thing—profit over people. 
Scale should be viewed as an opportunity. Not just to expand your client roster, but to offer employees more—more room to grow, more career opportunities, and more ways to make an impact. Growth isn’t a race to the top; it’s about building a better and more stable environment, in which teams are empowered to do their best work.
Doing so requires agencies to think strategically, focusing their efforts on the industries, clients, or projects that align with their goals, and releasing the rest—to grow with purpose.
1. Consider Both the Near- and Long-Term
Growth isn’t always linear. Pay attention to market conditions, using them to determine when stability is more valuable than scale. Evaluate what appear to be quick wins through the lens of your long-term vision.
2. Establish Clear Boundaries
Know which industries and clients align with your values, and equally important—be clear about who you won’t work with. Defining these boundaries keeps your team focused and fosters long-term partnerships.
3. Don't Be Afraid to Say No
Meeting a client’s needs doesn’t always mean saying “yes.” In fact, your answer should often be “no,” “maybe,” or “what if we thought about this differently?” If you're not the right fit, say so—clients will appreciate your honesty, and come back to when the time is right.
4. Invest in Your People
Your team is your greatest asset. Invest in their growth, celebrate their wins, and encourage their personal development. Prioritizing your people increases their intrinsic motivation, which drives company success.
5. Embrace Adaptation and Different Perspectives
Continuously iterate on your services, team structures, and growth strategies. Solicit feedback from across the organization, especially among employees with non-traditional backgrounds—fresh ideas that will push your business forward.
At the end of the day, we don't just scale for the sake of scaling—we do it to build a better, more impactful business for our team, our clients, and the world around us. That shift in perspective makes all the difference.

Growth isn’t always linear. Pay attention to market conditions, using them to determine when stability is more valuable than scale. Evaluate what appear to be quick wins through the lens of your long-term vision.

2\. Establish Clear Boundaries

Know which industries and clients align with your values, and equally important—be clear about who you won’t work with. Defining these boundaries keeps your team focused and fosters long-term partnerships.

3\. Don't Be Afraid to Say No

Meeting a client’s needs doesn’t always mean saying “yes.” In fact, your answer should often be “no,” “maybe,” or “what if we thought about this differently?” If you're not the right fit, say so—clients will appreciate your honesty, and come back to when the time is right.

4\. Invest in Your People

Your team is your greatest asset. Invest in their growth, celebrate their wins, and encourage their personal development. Prioritizing your people increases their intrinsic motivation, which drives company success.

5\. Embrace Adaptation and Different Perspectives

Continuously iterate on your services, team structures, and growth strategies. Solicit feedback from across the organization, especially among employees with non-traditional backgrounds—fresh ideas that will push your business forward.

At the end of the day, we don't just scale for the sake of scaling—we do it to build a better, more impactful business for our team, our clients, and the world around us. That shift in perspective makes all the difference.

Custom AI Tools to Elevate and Accelerate Client Work
Building new tools 
for today’s needs.
How
AI-powered
customization
elevates

Article_Building_new_creative_tools_HERO from Instrument on Vimeo 
For a long time, brand systems came in one form: final, fixed, often trapped in a PDF. You’d design it once, hand it off, and hope for the best. They had rules and grids and sometimes a friendly “how not to use the logo” page. And for a while, that was enough.
But that model doesn’t hold up anymore. 
Today, brands live in motion. They flex across formats, devices, regions, and teams. What once felt durable now feels rigid. The speed of culture has outpaced the tools we used to document it. 
At
Instrument,
we’ve
always
been
drawn
to
the
friction—the
moments
where
a
bit
of
invention
can
unlock
something
bigger.
That’s especially true when it comes to scaling design systems, where creativity and repetition exist in a constant push and pull. 
There’s been a lot of noise about AI—what it means for creativity, for craft, for the future of design. But useful applications—the kind that quietly enhance the work rather than overhaul it—are still surprisingly rare. So we’re building our own.
We’re experimenting with emerging tech to see how it can scale, accelerate, and even elevate the creative process—without compromising what matters: taste, clarity, and intent. To us, these aren’t just tools—they’re instruments of the industry’s future. Let us introduce you to a few of them.
Starting with Friction
In a recent rebrand for a legacy fashion retailer (more on that soon), we developed a custom layout tool that automates and scales design across sizes and ratios. Powered by a model that’s trained on a robust brand identity system and a series of intelligent inputs, the tool allows the in-house team to roll out the rebrand faster and at scale—without losing consistency or creative integrity.
Not to remove the human touch, but to protect it. As designers, we wanted to keep the inventing part—the thinking, the experimentation, the taste—firmly in human hands. When you’re not stuck adjusting margins or resizing templates, you can focus on shaping how a brand actually lives in the world.
We paired that with a brand voice assistant that helps generate everything from product copy to newsletters and social posts. It gets smarter over time, learning from feedback and evolving to match the brand’s tone—confident, aspirational, precise. It’s not just a shortcut. It’s a way to preserve the craft of writing, even as the content demands grow.
When we identify repetitive production tasks and create tools that anyone can use with minimal training, we democratize the creative process. This approach frees us up to focus on innovative work that truly moves brands forward—ultimately creating greater impact for our clients and their customers.
Automation with intention
For the rebrand of an iconic entertainment company, we reduced the overhead of generating logo variations. Once the brand guardrails were set, we built a web app that allows anyone to create sub-brand logos—across colors and formats—using a simple text input.
We also created a Figma plugin that applies palette rules to an ever-expanding catalog of IP and automatically integrates the result into the design system. And we used AI to crop and position key art within consistent brand shapes online—transforming a once time-consuming task into something anyone can do in minutes. While similar tools exist, building bespoke models allows us to train and tailor the technology to the specific need, versus general use, which enhances the output.
For one of our social clients, we built a suite of tools to support designers, producers, and strategists alike. Parsing global analytics can be overwhelming, let alone turning them into creative insights. So we built a tool that analyzes every video in a campaign—over 2,000 so far—cross-referencing creative elements with technical data. This helps teams understand what’s working, and why, so they can make smarter, faster, data-informed decisions.
At the same time, we made transcreation easier by connecting localized content variations directly into Figma—so the right version is always just a click away.
At the end of the day, it’s all about problem- solving. These common challenges—like scale, adaptability or consistency—might stay the same, but the way we think about solving them is ever-evolving. That’s what keeps us on our toes.
Jack De CaluweGroup Executive Creative Director
This isn't in the brief. (And that's the point.)
The most meaningful solutions often emerge in the margins—in the space between what's asked and what's needed. None of these solutions were in the brief. They were born out of friction—of seeing the same bottlenecks show up again and again. At Instrument, we’ve addressed this by embedding creative technologists into our project teams—folks who bring fresh perspectives and inventive solves others might overlook. They sit shoulder-to-shoulder with designers, writers, and strategists, looking for unexpected ways to remove friction and unlock flow.
Their role isn’t to chase novelty for novelty’s sake. It’s to build things that make the work better. Sharper. Faster, yes—but also more thoughtful. More consistent. More alive.
Because the truth is, these aren’t just technical solutions. They’re creative ones. They carve out space for human judgment. For taste. For experimentation. For the kinds of ideas you can’t automate.
That’s what we’re investing in. Not just better tools—but better conditions for creativity to thrive—for our teams, and for the clients who trust us to push the work further.

Oura
This is tagged with: product
Oura is the leading smart ring on the market—but as competition grows, being first isn’t enough. Together with the Oura team, we redesigned their website experience to transform how customers discover, learn about, and shop the product online.
Oura Ring Website Case Study | Hero Video from Instrument on Vimeo 
People have more options than ever when choosing wearable technology to support their health and fitness goals. They are looking for answers that are as diverse as the industry itself. How might Oura tell their complex story, beautifully?
By showing, not telling.
Storytelling that converts
Leveraging existing user research and data, we set out to design an e-commerce experience that matches consumer’s needs and mental models. To maximize the impact of the insights we already had, we weaved a golden thread through their personas—prioritizing shared attributes and drivers to design an experience to reach, captivate, and convert the most people. 

The science and technology behind Oura’s product is as impressive as it is expansive, and to tell this story effectively, we re-imagined the site’s information architecture, content, and navigation to provide shoppers with better learning and purchasing journeys. Our own qualitative and quantitative testing both confirmed that shoppers crave rich storytelling that inspires curiosity and trust, and further honed our creative output.
From beginning to end, the new site puts people at the center. To get there, our team wore the ring, worked closely with Oura’s in-house experts to understand why their product stands out and ahead of the rest, and iteratively tested our strategy and designs with real consumers.
Progressive disclosure
Oura Ring reads and translates the body’s most meaningful and complex messages to help us transform how we feel every day—without overwhelming us. 

The foundation of our design system is progressive disclosure, leveraging layers of information, animation, and micro-interactions to help people understand the big picture behind Oura’s science and design, while providing pathways to dig deeper into the details that are most relevant in their lives. 

Throughout our process and the final site, we drew inspiration from the emotional and tactical moments that come when you wear the ring. We layered Oura’s in-app UI, data visualization, lifestyle and CGI photography, and rich storytelling to represent Oura’s many complex features and benefits. Ultimately, these moments anchor the most important points in a consumer’s path to purchase with dynamic interactions and delight.
A rich and scalable system
Oura’s new website design is as immersive as it is repeatable. We aimed to strike a balance between a unique experience and a system with reusable pages and components. Thus, enabling cohesion and continuity for both consumers and Oura’s internal teams as the brand and product offering continues to evolve.
One month after launch, the numbers speak for themselves:
42% increase in sales per day
130% mobile performance

By far and away the best agency I have ever worked with. The expertise, the leadership, the humility, the creativity–everything you guys have done has been really phenomenal.

# Redesigning Ouraring.com | Instrument

## Oura

This is tagged with: product

#### Oura is the leading smart ring on the market—but as competition grows, being first isn’t enough. Together with the Oura team, we redesigned their website experience to transform how customers discover, learn about, and shop the product online.

   Oura Ring Website Case Study | Hero Video from Instrument on Vimeo

People have more options than ever when choosing wearable technology to support their health and fitness goals. They are looking for answers that are as diverse as the industry itself. How might Oura tell their complex story, beautifully?

By showing, not telling.

## Storytelling that converts

Leveraging existing user research and data, we set out to design an e-commerce experience that matches consumer’s needs and mental models. To maximize the impact of the insights we already had, we weaved a golden thread through their personas—prioritizing shared attributes and drivers to design an experience to reach, captivate, and convert the most people.  
  
The science and technology behind Oura’s product is as impressive as it is expansive, and to tell this story effectively, we re-imagined the site’s information architecture, content, and navigation to provide shoppers with better learning and purchasing journeys. Our own qualitative and quantitative testing both confirmed that shoppers crave rich storytelling that inspires curiosity and trust, and further honed our creative output.

From beginning to end, the new site puts people at the center. To get there, our team wore the ring, worked closely with Oura’s in-house experts to understand why their product stands out and ahead of the rest, and iteratively tested our strategy and designs with real consumers.

## Progressive disclosure

Oura Ring reads and translates the body’s most meaningful and complex messages to help us transform how we feel every day—without overwhelming us.  
  
The foundation of our design system is progressive disclosure, leveraging layers of information, animation, and micro-interactions to help people understand the big picture behind Oura’s science and design, while providing pathways to dig deeper into the details that are most relevant in their lives.  
  
Throughout our process and the final site, we drew inspiration from the emotional and tactical moments that come when you wear the ring. We layered Oura’s in-app UI, data visualization, lifestyle and CGI photography, and rich storytelling to represent Oura’s many complex features and benefits. Ultimately, these moments anchor the most important points in a consumer’s path to purchase with dynamic interactions and delight.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/1920x992/e16d14fb70/oura-smart-ring-mobile-screen-shots.png/m/)

## A rich and scalable system

Oura’s new website design is as immersive as it is repeatable. We aimed to strike a balance between a unique experience and a system with reusable pages and components. Thus, enabling cohesion and continuity for both consumers and Oura’s internal teams as the brand and product offering continues to evolve.

One month after launch, the numbers speak for themselves:

*   42% increase in sales per day
*   130% mobile performance
*   3% increase in funnel progression

> ### By far and away the best agency I have ever worked with. The expertise, the leadership, the humility, the creativity–everything you guys have done has been really phenomenal.

### Our Roles

#### Strategy

*   Consumer Research
*   Audience Insights & Definition
*   User Story Mapping
*   Qualitative & Quantitative User Testing
*   Information Architecture
*   UX Strategy

#### Design

*   UX Design
*   Responsive Design
*   Prototyping
*   Creative Direction
*   Art Direction
*   Motion Design

#### Content

*   Content Strategy
*   Key Messaging
*   Voice & Tone
*   Copywriting
*   Post Production
*   Sound Design

2024 Transparency Report | Instrument
2024 Transparency Report
At Instrument, transparency is the foundation of how we operate, engage, and evolve. It means not only celebrating our progress but also being open about the areas we’re focusing on and how we plan to address them. Our annual transparency report reflects on these efforts and serves as a roadmap for the future, sharing our representation data and the steps we're taking to create positive change within our organization and the communities we serve.
Here’s a quick summary of our annual data, with the option to download the full report if you’d like to dive deeper.
*Please note that all percentage points have been rounded to the nearest whole number.
2024 Goals, Actions, & Outcomes
Actions & Outcomes
Public ED&I Commitment: We launched a new ED&I webpage to reaffirm our ongoing commitment, even as other companies scale back.
Talent Review Enhancements: We introduced a more thorough talent review process to improve fairness and consistency, with manager training, leadership roundtables, and a simpler review template.
Expanded Representation Metrics: Employees can now anonymously identify as LGBTQ+, disabled, neurodiverse, or chronically ill in our engagement surveys.
Hybrid Working Model Exploration: We're shaping a hybrid work model that balances a great employee experience with top-tier performance.
Cultural Insights Council Pilot: We launched a pilot platform for employees to share diverse perspectives, helping shape marketing strategies, campaigns, and design.
Pro Bono Program Refresh: Through “Build Week,” teams worked with local BIPOC-owned businesses in Portland to tackle challenges and find growth opportunities.
Equity & Inclusion Favorability
Employee sentiment on equity and inclusion dipped for the first time since 2020, mainly due to the return-to-office mandate. In response, we reversed the policy and pivoted to a hybrid model that balances flexibility with in-person collaboration to drive innovation and help everyone thrive.
BIPOC Representation
BIPOC representation increased at the leadership level but decreased slightly at the company-wide level. We’re actively analyzing these trends to identify solutions for improving representation.
Gender Representation
In 2024, we announced our first all-women C-suite, a big step in strengthening our commitment to diverse leadership. This milestone builds on our recognition as one of Fast Company’s Best Workplaces for Women Innovators, and we continue to foster diverse perspectives at the top.
Pay Equity
Pay equity remains in line with industry benchmarks, though we identified a 9.7% salary variance for Black or African American leadership employees, driven by recent promotions and changes in 2024. 
This year, we also introduced a new metric—employee promotion velocity—that tracks the average time for advancement. This ensures career development is fair, consistent, and accessible. Our findings show employees are promoted within a consistent timeframe, with no gaps exceeding six months. While minor timing differences exist, the maximum promotion interval is six months, falling within our target range of 6 to 12 months.
Looking ahead
Transparency builds trust, and this report reflects our commitment to continuous improvement and accountability at every level. As we look to 2025, a pivotal year for Instrument, our goals extend beyond demographic benchmarks. We’ll reflect on our progress and refine our equity vision for 2026-2030 while focusing on the following actions:
Fostering psychological safety, enhancing employee engagement, and strengthening accountability across all levels.

# 2024 Transparency Report | Instrument

**2024** Transparency Report

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/1920x1080/008ff1ab92/inst_transparency_report_2023-24_wide_1218.jpg/m/)

At Instrument, transparency is the foundation of how we operate, engage, and evolve. It means not only celebrating our progress but also being open about the areas we’re focusing on and how we plan to address them. Our annual transparency report reflects on these efforts and serves as a roadmap for the future, sharing our representation data and the steps we're taking to create positive change within our organization and the communities we serve.

Here’s a quick summary of our annual data, with the option to download the full report if you’d like to dive deeper.

_\*Please note that all percentage points have been rounded to the nearest whole number._

2024 Goals, Actions, & Outcomes

Actions & Outcomes

*   **Public ED&I Commitment**: We launched a new ED&I webpage to reaffirm our ongoing commitment, even as other companies scale back.
*   **Talent Review Enhancements**: We introduced a more thorough talent review process to improve fairness and consistency, with manager training, leadership roundtables, and a simpler review template.
*   **Expanded Representation Metrics**: Employees can now anonymously identify as LGBTQ+, disabled, neurodiverse, or chronically ill in our engagement surveys.
*   **Hybrid Working Model Exploration**: We're shaping a hybrid work model that balances a great employee experience with top-tier performance.
*   **Cultural Insights Council Pilot**: We launched a pilot platform for employees to share diverse perspectives, helping shape marketing strategies, campaigns, and design.
*   **Pro Bono Program Refresh:** Through “Build Week,” teams worked with local BIPOC-owned businesses in Portland to tackle challenges and find growth opportunities.

### Equity & Inclusion Favorability

Employee sentiment on equity and inclusion dipped for the first time since 2020, mainly due to the return-to-office mandate. In response, we reversed the policy and pivoted to a hybrid model that balances flexibility with in-person collaboration to drive innovation and help everyone thrive.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/838x777/128f869904/group-2055244983_2.svg)

### BIPOC Representation

BIPOC representation increased at the leadership level but decreased slightly at the company-wide level. We’re actively analyzing these trends to identify solutions for improving representation.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/838x777/0f3a75a42b/bipocgroup.svg)

### Gender Representation

In 2024, we announced our first all-women C-suite, a big step in strengthening our commitment to diverse leadership. This milestone builds on our recognition as one of [Fast Company’s Best Workplaces for Women Innovators](https://www.instrument.com/latest/instrument-recognized-as-a-best-workplace-for-women-innovators), and we continue to foster diverse perspectives at the top.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/838x777/287340a462/femalegroup.svg)

### Pay Equity

Pay equity remains in line with industry benchmarks, though we identified a 9.7% salary variance for Black or African American leadership employees, driven by recent promotions and changes in 2024.

This year, we also introduced a new metric—employee promotion velocity—that tracks the average time for advancement. This ensures career development is fair, consistent, and accessible. Our findings show employees are promoted within a consistent timeframe, with no gaps exceeding six months. While minor timing differences exist, the maximum promotion interval is six months, falling within our target range of 6 to 12 months.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1004432/838x528/471be188e3/payequity2.svg)

## Looking ahead

Transparency builds trust, and this report reflects our commitment to continuous improvement and accountability at every level. As we look to 2025, a pivotal year for Instrument, our goals extend beyond demographic benchmarks. We’ll reflect on our progress and refine our equity vision for 2026-2030 while focusing on the following actions:

*   Fostering psychological safety, enhancing employee engagement, and strengthening accountability across all levels.
*   Training teams to leverage the Cultural Insights Council as a platform for gathering diverse perspectives that inform our marketing strategies, campaigns, and design.
*   Refining our hybrid work strategy to lead by example, demonstrating that agencies can thrive through people-first innovation and bold action.
*   Applying our expertise in branding, marketing, and product development to deliver creative solutions and drive impactful growth at the community level through Build Week.

To protect individual privacy, we have chosen not to show data for groups that have less than 3 individuals in them.

**What is a role level?**

To protect privacy and provide meaningful data, we’ve grouped pay bands into "role levels," each covering a range of experience years. Without this, we'd need to hide more data to safeguard privacy.

text:
What we're reading | Latest
What We’re Reading: Our Fall '22 Book Club Picks
Homelatest
What We're Reading: Our Fall '22 Book Club Picks
At Instrument, we’re big on reading: We gift books to our designers and writers over the holidays, and we love sharing our latest reads and recommendations in our #books Slack channel. For us, reading is a vital part of exhibiting a growth mindset — one of our core values — which we embrace by continually working to expand our capabilities and cultural awareness. 
So at the end of summer, we launched a book club within our creative discipline to get folks talking, sharing ideas, and thinking about our craft. After all, what better way to connect and spark conversations than over a wonderful new book? 
Our writers and designers were given the chance to select from a reading list before gathering at the end of the summer to discuss their books of choice in breakout rooms. Selections ranged from chunky anthologies of creative work to tactical manuals, and the resulting discussions were lively explorations of what we do — and how we can do it better. 
Here’s what we read, and a bit of what we learned.
Writing Is Designing: Words and the User Experience
In Writing Is Designing, authors Michael J. Metts and Andy Welfle make the case for why writing is critical to designing clear, usable UI. 
As a designer, there’s a tendency sometimes to think of writing as supplemental to design, when it's really an integral part of what makes design effective at communication.
Writing Is Designing (Left), Black Futures (Right)
Throughout the book, the authors drop in useful tips for stronger, more accessible writing; words of wisdom for better collaboration; and tales from their own careers as content strategists and UX writers. While geared toward writers, the book is relevant for anyone in looking to build better, more user-friendly products. 
“Writing is Designing is written from a UX perspective, but the basic tenets of clear communication can (and should!) apply to every discipline in our field — not just writers and designers, but strategists and producers,” says senior writer Sammi Chancey. “I would recommend the book to anyone looking for a how-to guide for making smart, thoughtful work.” 
Black Futures
This anthology, curated by Kimberly Drew and Jenna Wortham, compiles impactful and inspirational works of Black creators. 
“This is definitely a book that encourages you to read in a different way, as I often found myself leaping in and out of different stories,” says designer Suvani Dave. “It’s a book that is not traditionally linear, with a start and end, but instead a timeless and continuous collection.” 
Ranging from essays to conversations with artists and activists to infographics and Instagram posts, Black Futures paints a vibrant picture of what it is to be “Black and alive right now.” 
“The most compelling thing within this book is how these stories are filled with photos, narratives, interviews, tweets and snapshots, cementing Black people in the digital age,” Dave says. “It celebrates and commemorates a few of the Black voices that have made impacts over that past 20-plus years.”
I love Taking a Line for a Walk because the prompts spark the reader to think across hundreds of entirely new ways for exploring creative possibilities.
Nishat AkhtarVP of Creative
Taking A Line For A Walk (Left), The Politics Of Design (Right)
Taking a Line for a Walk: Assignments in Design Education
In this compendium of 224 educational prompts, editors Nina Paim and Emilia Bergmark examine design education through the lens of pedagogical assignments. As a collective, the assignments serve as fodder for conversations around how we develop design talent in the classroom. 
“Taking a Line for a Walk takes you out of the box to creatively explore, consider, and experiment with the environment around you, or to uncover the unexpected through prompts of all kinds,” says Nishat Akhtar, VP of Creative.
The Politics of Design: A (Not So) Global Design Manual for Visual Communication
Designers’ work may be created with a specific audience in mind, but it has the potential to reach people all over the world — which makes it all the more critical that creatives understand how the symbols, images, typefaces, and colors they incorporate into their designs will resonate with audiences across cultures. In Politics of Design, author Ruben Pater has collected examples that help illustrate this need for visual literacy, while providing insights into stronger visual communication. 
“The underlying premise of the book is that design is never neutral nor objective. The visual artifacts we create — whether we recognize it or not — are imbued with historical, cultural and political connotations,” says senior designer Michael Lo.
As I read through Politics of Design, I was reminded that design does not live in isolation. It is important to carefully consider the cultural context that our work is situated in.
Michael LoSenior Designer
Living With Complexity (Left), Strategy Is Your Words (Right)
Living with Complexity
In Living with Complexity, Nielsen Norman Group co-founder Donald A. Norman rejects the concept that technology is overly complex and in need of simplifying. 
“My takeaway is that in design, trying to achieve simplicity for simplicity's sake is not always the best solution, primarily because people tend to crave some level of complexity,” says associate design director Kara Smarsh. “When something is too simple it becomes boring or worse, too limited in function to be useful.” 
Norman extols the virtues of that which is complicated, rich, and meaningful — putting the onus on designers to make complexity more digestible, rather than overcomplicating things through poor design.
“We should strive to allow things to be appropriately complex for their subject matter or intent, to use natural signifiers (which might be otherwise termed ‘user behaviors’ in our field of work), and other thoughtful methods of design to create useful tools that enrich our experiences,” Smarsh says. 
Strategy is Your Words
In this 400-page deep dive, author Mark Pollard unpacks the mind of a strategist, examines some of strategists’ biggest (and most damaging) buzzwords, and argues that strategy should be viewed as creative work. Strategy is Your Words also includes Pollard’s “The Four Points” framework, to help strategists better identify problems, define their insights, explain their ideas, work with other creatives, and run more efficient workshops. 
“I appreciated how Pollard urges creatives to chase down and interrogate good ideas — and to remember that, rather than being the focus of our work, stuffy frameworks and jargon are, as Pollard says, ‘simply tools available to use when you have handiwork to do,’” says senior writer Erik Henriksen. 
… and so much more
While this may have been our first official fall book club at Instrument, it certainly won’t be our last. Reading together, diving into these great minds, and discussing the impact on our work was time well spent. 
"It was reinvigorating to spend dedicated time with our teammates from across the agency and across creative disciplines to discuss outside work that’s shedding new light on the way our industry is evolving, along with the way we do our jobs,” says writing lead Evan P. Schneider. 
Until next time, we hope our reading list above inspires some deep thinking and memorable conversations. Stay tuned for the next iteration of “What We’re Reading Now” at Instrument!
